newsitem.title: SPAIN: Wall St drags Madrid stocks down, but support seen.
newsitem.headline: Wall St drags Madrid stocks down, but support seen.

text.p: Madrid stocks closed lower on Friday, dragged by losses on Wall Street and profit-taking in Repsol, dealers said.
But they said sellers were reluctant as many predict a cut in interest rates next week after March inflation came in at the low end of expectations, supporting the bourse.
The general index fell 3.60 points, 0.75 percent, to 475.46 and the Ibex shed 46.94 points, 0.86 percent, 5,441.35.
Repsol dropped 80 pesetas to 6,070 after an all-time high hit on Thursday prompted investors to take profits. The stock had risen "simply too high too fast" this week, one trader said.
Telefonica fell 10 pesetas to 3,415, amid substantial interest from U.S. funds, dealers said. The market is awaiting news on its choice of a U.S partner, widely expected to be MCI.
Spain inflation, which was 2.2 percent in March versus 2.5 percent in February, raised expectations of a cut in key rates at Tuesday's regular repo auction.

"The CPI supported us today, although we couldn't ignore the trend in the U.S. But people aren't willing to sell in case we do get a rate cut," said a dealer at Central Hispano Bolsa, adding that the firm expects a 25 basis point cut.
